        ### Question
        In a colon cancer screening program, a 52-year-old patient undergoes a colonoscopy. The entire colon is normal in appearance, except for the finding of a 2 cm pedicled sigmoid polyp that is removed with a diathermy loop. The anatomopathological result indicates that there is carcinoma "in situ" limited to the head of the polyp. He has a thoracoabdominal CT reported as normal. Indicate what would be the correct conduct to follow:

        ### Options
        opa. Segmental resection of the affected colon.
opb. Periodic endoscopic surveillance.
opc. Local resection of the base of the polyp.
opd. Sigmoidectomy plus lymphadenectomy.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "2 cm pedicled sigmoid polyp" -> "carcinoma in situ at the head of the polyp" -> "no invasion beyond the polyp" -> "local resection is sufficient" -> "periodic endoscopic surveillance may be needed" -> 85%
CHAIN: "2 cm pedicled sigmoid polyp" -> "carcinoma in situ" -> "no lymph node involvement" -> "local resection of the base of the polyp is appropriate" -> "low risk of metastasis" -> 90%
CHAIN: "carcinoma in situ" -> "localized cancer" -> "no need for extensive surgery" -> "local resection is adequate" -> "monitoring for recurrence is important" -> 80%
CHAIN: "carcinoma in situ" -> "normal thoracoabdominal CT" -> "no evidence of spread" -> "local resection of the polyp base is indicated" -> "follow-up with surveillance colonoscopy" -> 88%
